reports.provenance_limit: Claims are pinned to PTI README and the SYCL event reference but were not independently source-verified in this review. The report itself flags that the loaded-runtime mapping belongs to a different binary; the current binary's loaded libraries, driver/IGC identities and unitrace build/version still need per-run proof. reports.main_correction_to_retain: Use per-instance timing only after current binary/runtime/profiler identity and source-symbol mapping are pinned. cross_report_assessment.novelty_and_redundancy: R777 closes the safe kernel-attribution method-selection gap left by R675/R726/R733/R748 and is decision support rather than a local profile. R778 centers sparse matrix storage/conversion amortization, distinct from the earlier scheduling/residency reports, but has a bibliographic retrieval defect. R779 centers transaction sectors, page translation and dependent gathers; it is adjacent to earlier graph and SLM work but adds a separate mechanism-level comparison. R778 and R779 are not duplicates of each other.
cross_report_assessment.applicability_and_evidence_limits: All three were read-only research. R777 supplies a useful method choice, not current-stack qualification or timings. R778/R779 are literature and design references only; none establishes B570 performance, a local bottleneck, adoption, or a code direction. Main need not ingest either collection report now.
cross_report_assessment.dispatch_correction: For the immediate QSA attribution choice, retrieve only R777's Method comparison and Recommendation and minimum evidence sections. Do not dispatch another generic head8/head-tile/SLM study: R568, R605 and R747 already cover that geometry, and the new isolated result rejects it while leaving cause unmeasured. Wait for the pinned KV-sharing proposal or a fresh per-kernel attribution result before creating any attention-mechanism or counter follow-up. Do not reopen the resolved colon-delimiter configuration failure absent new evidence.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Retaining KV reuse while distributing long-query attention work
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: After Main reviews and pins the new independent source proposal, compare a work-group that reuses one staged KV tile across multiple query-head tiles with the already tested two-work-group head split and with sequence-tile parallelism that merges partial online-softmax state. Which conditions on live FP32 accumulators, register/SLM footprint, barriers, duplicated loads, available parallelism and merge scratch determine whether each decomposition can win? Identify the minimum counter evidence that can distinguish these costs without assuming a cause for the rejected head8 regression.
next_three_research_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Use original attention papers and current SYCL/joint-matrix documentation. Compare at least three decompositions, include cases where retaining one KV tile increases live state or lowers parallelism, and distinguish CUDA-era paper results from Arc/SYCL. Do not restate the already reviewed head8 arithmetic/index blueprint or claim that the observed regression has a known cause. No source code, local measurements or implementation recommendation.
next_three_research_scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 words; at most six substantive sources; one comparison table and a bounded evidence plan.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisites: The current KV-sharing source proposal must be complete, immutably pinned and reviewed by Main; a distinct unresolved method question must remain after comparing it with R568/R605/R747. This is a public-source decision-support review, not a request to inspect the proposal's implementation.
next_three_research_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: Current assignment reports the prior head8+4 prototype as oracle-clean but 2.85x/3.16x slower and rejected; the cause is not measured. A new KV-preserving proposal is only under consideration and has no pinned result in the supplied status. R568/R605/R747 already describe head splitting and duplicated KV work, so dispatch before the new proposal could only repeat known alternatives.

next_three_research_scopes.title: Atomic fan-in strategies under degree skew in GPU graph aggregation
next_three_research_scopes.finite_question: For non-LLM GPU graph workloads with skewed degree and changing frontier density, compare destination-centric pull, edge-centric atomic push, warp/work-group-local aggregation, and segmented reduction. How do contention, duplicate destinations, frontier sparsity, temporary storage, determinism and accumulation order change the crossover, and what measured counterexamples favor the simpler path?

Compare at least three strategies across low/high degree skew and sparse/dense active frontiers. Keep the center on atomic fan-in and reduction semantics; do not repeat R759 work partitioning/scans, R763 pipeline/data residency, R778 storage conversion, or R779 cache/page transaction mechanisms. Do not propose a Strata change or make an Arc performance claim.

next_three_research_scopes.prerequisites: Public source access only; no local workload or device result is required.
